scratch_note: patch applied at the stamped revision in a scratch worktree; this commit is on no branch and is not pushed
property: In MultiPartParser.parse(), any Content-Disposition filename must pass through sanitize_file_name(), which unescapes HTML entities first, strips Windows-style backslash paths second, and applies os.path.basename() last, so no encoded or literal path-separator sequence can survive into the value used to construct filesystem paths.
vulnerability: MultiPartParser.parse() applied os.path.basename() to the raw Content-Disposition filename before HTML-unescaping it, so an attacker could HTML-entity-encode path separators (e.g. '../') to slip '../' sequences past the basename check; after unescaping, the resulting filename contained real path traversal sequences that could be passed to upload handlers writing to the filesystem.

completeness.protected_value: the client-supplied upload filename obtained from the Content-Disposition header in MultiPartParser.parse() (disposition.get('filename'))

covered.reason: The only consumer of the raw disposition filename in this file is the call `handler.new_file(field_name, file_name, content_type, content_length, charset, content_type_extra)` at line ~234-237. The fix diff inserts `file_name = self.sanitize_file_name(file_name)` (line 216) before this call and before the `if not file_name: continue` check, so file_name passed to handlers is always fully unescaped, backslash-stripped, and basename-applied: `file_name = force_str(file_name, encoding, errors='replace')` then `file_name = self.sanitize_file_name(file_name)`.

These receive file_name only via the new_file() call from MultiPartParser.parse(), which already passes the sanitized value (`self.file_name = file_name` at line 101, then used to construct `TemporaryUploadedFile(self.file_name, ...)` at line 147 and `InMemoryUploadedFile(..., name=self.file_name, ...)` at line 203); no separate raw filename path exists here.
Receives the already-sanitized file_name from the handler chain and additionally re-applies `os.path.basename(name)` (line 42) as defense-in-depth, so this consumer is doubly covered.

completeness.value_note: Single string value extracted at multipartparser.py line 213 (file_name = disposition.get('filename')), then decoded and sanitized before being handed to upload handlers.
completeness.context_note: The excerpts show the full parse() method flow from disposition.get('filename') through sanitize_file_name() to handler.new_file(), and trace file_name through the only two upload handler implementations into UploadedFile's name setter, which is the complete set of filesystem-path-relevant consumers of this value shown in the repo. Other files referencing 'basename'/'unescape'/'file_name' (loaddata, dumpdata, makemessages, html.py, staticfiles/utils.py, management/base.py, response.py, etc.) operate on unrelated values (fixture names, prog names, URLs in linkify, static file paths, download filenames) and are not consumers of the Content-Disposition upload filename, so they are correctly out of scope for this fix.

cannot_verify: This contract only verifies the ordering within sanitize_file_name() and its single call site in parse(); it cannot verify that downstream upload handlers (e.g. custom new_file() implementations) don't perform additional unsafe path construction with the sanitized name, nor does it cover other Django versions/branches or non-multipart file-upload code paths outside this file. Consumers outside this repository (third-party packages, deployment configuration) are not examined; the consumer list is only as complete as the symbol references the query was shown.
